requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to boot with the kernel parameter audit=1 and retain it across reboots.
requirements.summary: The GRUB kernel stanza was updated with exactly one audit=1 parameter. A bounded reboot changed the boot identity, after which /proc/cmdline and GRUB still contained audit=1 exactly once; kernel messages and auditctl directly confirmed auditing was enabled with no lost records.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using an implementation compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after the change and reboot, the system remained CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5. The executor used the existing GRUB Legacy configuration and native service/shutdown utilities, with no evidence of package, release, or kernel replacement.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct pre/post observations and a completed reboot demonstrate persistent audit=1 operation while preserving CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5. The provider-wide restart protocol is strong: it captures a healthy pre-restart root filesystem and SSH service, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered SSH, auditd, filesystem, configuration checksum, and sentinel data.
limitations: The lifecycle collector does not inventory /boot/grub or /var/tmp, so it cannot independently establish whether the GRUB backup, persistence sentinel, and reboot log remained after verification.

The lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum command both before and after execution, so package consistency was not substantively measured; however, the executor timeline contains no package-management mutation.
Systemd failed-unit collection was unsupported on this legacy SysV-init platform; direct post-reboot checks nevertheless showed sshd and auditd running.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was established. The GRUB backup and edit in cmd-b23cbf2b435746fd supported safe implementation and rollback; the persistence sentinel in cmd-63b30e64072141e7 supported mandatory restart data-recovery evidence; and the detached reboot/log redirection in cmd-00a4c7a146ac4841 supported the required restart. Read-only discovery and temporary connectivity failures were not mutations. Lifecycle comparison showed no new /tmp entries, platform drift, socket exposure, or observable package-health regression. The evidence does not show whether the retained GRUB backup, /var/tmp sentinel, and reboot log were subsequently cleaned, creating minor residue uncertainty, but each had a clear evidence-supported purpose.
